scalesUsed.application: The tonal framework for John Frusciante's relentless sixteenth-note alternate picked main riff
The relative major key underpinning the triumphant chorus and vocal harmonies

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Tour-de-force alternate-picking endurance anthem combining classical triad voice-leading with clean Stratocaster chime
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: G# minor is the relative minor of B major

mainProgression.description: The iconic four-chord pop/rock cycle (i - VI - III - VII) rendered as rapid arpeggiated hammer-on/pull-off dyads.

sectionProgressions.description: Continuous sixteenth-note alternate picked arpeggios with hammer-ons and pull-offs on strings 3 and 4
Broad strummed barre and open chords under the soaring vocal hook
Emotional minor bridge moving into Hendrix-style wah guitar solo fills

harmonicFunction: G#m (i) - Minor tonic anchoring the relentless circular motion
E (VI) - Major submediant adding emotional lift and warmth
B (III) - Relative major providing bright harmonic sunshine
F# (VII) - Subtonic dominant chord driving smoothly back into G#m

techniques.name: Relentless Alternate Picking & Hammer-On/Pull-Off Stamina
techniques.description: Maintaining strict down-up-down-up alternate picking at 104 BPM across string crosses while executing rapid hammer-ons and pull-offs on every beat

notes: G#m shape: Bass on 6th fret D string, hammer-on/pull-off 4h6p4 on G string
E shape: Bass on 6th fret A string, hammer-on/pull-off 4h6p4 on G string
B shape: Bass on 7th fret low E string, hammer-on/pull-off 4h6p4 on G string
F# shape: Bass on 6th fret low E string, hammer-on/pull-off 4h6p4 on G string
sequence: Pick down on the bass note on string 4, 5, or 6
Pick up on the 4th fret G string
Hammer on with ring finger to 6th fret, pull off back to 4th fret
Maintain strict right-hand alternate picking with zero forearm tension
Repeat continuously for 5 minutes without missing a beat
tips: Start at 60 BPM with a metronome and ONLY speed up when your right wrist is completely loose
Use a light gauge pick (.60mm Dunlop Tortex) to glide smoothly across strings
Frusciante used his vintage '62 Strat into Marshall Major clean channels for sparkling articulation

techniques.name: Dynamic Open-Chord Strumming & Relative Major Voicings
techniques.description: Switching from intricate high-speed alternate-picked arpeggios to sweeping, resonant open-chord and barre strumming during the anthemic B major chorus

notes: Dynamic release: The chorus opens up into full strummed acoustic/electric power
Vocal support: Strumming locks tightly with Anthony Kiedis and John Frusciante's two-part harmonies
sequence: Anticipate the chorus explosion on beat 1 with an unmuted downstroke on G#m
Strum continuous eighth notes with accented downstrokes on beats 2 and 4
Transition smoothly back to the fast alternate-picking hand position without losing momentum
Engage subtle bridge pickup overdrive or Boss DS-2 boost during the outro
tips: Let the open high E and B strings ring over the E major chord for expansive sonic width
Relax your fretting hand completely during the chorus strums to recover stamina for the verse riff
Use the volume knob on your guitar to control the gain difference between verse chime and chorus power

sections.name: Main Alternate-Picked Riff Intro
sections.description: One of the most famous and technically demanding guitar riffs of the 21st century.
notes: Strict down-up alternate picking throughout
Crisp hammer-on and pull-off on the 3rd (G) string
Keep the right wrist relaxed and economical

sections.name: Verse 1 Rapid String-Crossing Groove
sections.description: The vocal verse begins as Frusciante maintains the relentless sixteenth-note alternate-picking engine beneath Anthony Kiedis's vocal.
notes: Maintain absolute dynamic consistency across string crosses
Listen to Chad Smith's hi-hat for steady 104 BPM subdivision
Avoid tension in the picking forearm

sections.name: Chorus 1 Soaring Relative Major Strumming ('The more I see, the less I know')
sections.description: Full strummed chords providing dynamic contrast and physical relief from the intense picking riff.
notes: Open, ringing chord voicings
Accentuate beats 2 and 4
Smooth transition between E and B

sections.name: Verse 2 Layered Electric Textures & Flea Interplay
sections.technique: Precision Alternate Picking with Secondary Guitar
sections.description: Second verse featuring layered clean guitar lines and Flea's melodic bass counterpoint dancing beneath the main riff.
notes: Keep right-hand pick depth shallow to avoid snagging strings
Let the hammer-on/pull-off ring with equal velocity to picked notes
Dynamic breathing room during vocal breaths

sections.name: Bridge Harmonic Lift & Emotional Build
sections.description: Emotional shift to C#m adding dramatic tension before lifting back into the euphoric chorus hook.
notes: Staccato arpeggios opening up into full strumming
Gradual crescendo over four bars
Prepare left hand for rapid return to 16th-note alternate picking

sections.name: Outro Climax & Frusciante Wah Embellishments
sections.description: The transcendent finale where Frusciante plays the relentless alternate-picking riff while layering overdriven wah guitar leads all the way to the final chord.
notes: Peak physical endurance test at 104 BPM
Overdriven wah lead fills intercut over the riff
Sustain final G#m barre chord with studio decay

guitar.pickup: Neck/Middle single-coil position for sparkling, glass-like chime

amp.recommended: Marshall Major 200W blended with Marshall Silver Jubilee 2555

effects.distortion: Boss DS-2 Turbo Distortion (engaged for bridge solo swells)
effects.chorus: Boss CE-1 Chorus Ensemble (subtle vintage preamp coloration)
effects.other: Dunlop Tortex 0.60mm picks (essential for light string crossing)

beginner.title: Chorus Chords & Progression
steps: Learn the four fundamental chords: G#m, E, B, and F#
Practice steady strumming in eighth notes at 85 BPM
Internalize the i - VI - III - VII chord cycle

intermediate.title: Slow-Speed Riff Mechanics
steps: Practice the hammer-on/pull-off pattern isolated on the G string at 60 BPM
Coordinate the shifting bass notes on strings 4, 5, and 6
Maintain strict down-up alternate picking without pausing

advanced.title: Full-Speed Stamina (104 BPM)
steps: Build speed incrementally (60 → 75 → 90 → 104 BPM) using a metronome
Eliminate all forearm tension through relaxed wrist picking
Perform the entire 5.5-minute track with consistent articulation and zero fatigue

commonMistakes: Tensing the right arm or gripping the pick too tightly, leading to fatigue within 30 seconds
Using all-downstrokes instead of strict down-up-down-up alternate picking
Rushing the hammer-on/pull-off timing relative to the sixteenth-note grid
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Isolated 4h6p4 hammer-pull drill on G string at 70 BPM
10 minutes: Slow riff cycle (G#m → E → B → F#) at 75 BPM with metronome
5 minutes: Speed burst drill: 4 measures at 104 BPM, rest 4 measures
5 minutes: Chorus chord transitions and relaxation
focusAreas: Right-hand wrist relaxation and economy of motion
Clean string muting of unused strings
metronomeWork: Dedicate at least 15 minutes daily at 70 BPM before attempting full album tempo of 104 BPM
